cards.prose: Matthew counts the days for us. Six days after he said that some standing there would not taste of death till they saw the Son of Adam *coming in his kingdom*, he takes three of them up a high mountain apart, and his face shines as the sun before them. The promise is hardly cold when they are shown his glory.
cards.member_phrase: till they see the Son of Adam coming in his kingdom
cards.member_sentence: The saying just before the mountain: some of those standing there will see the Son of Adam in his kingdom before they die.

cards.prose: Matthew says *after six days*, and Sinai keeps the same count: *the cloud covered it six days: and the seventh day he called unto Moses out of the midst of the cloud* (Exodus 24:16). Here again a man goes up a mountain after six days, and again a cloud comes and a voice speaks out of it.
cards.member_phrase: WHOLE
cards.member_sentence: A cloud covers the mount of Yahuah (the LORD) when Moses goes up, the first of the mountain clouds this chapter answers.

cards.prose: At Sinai the people were told to wash their clothes and be ready, because Yahuah (the LORD) would come down on the mountain in the sight of all, and they were kept back from it. On this mountain three go up with Yahusha (Jesus), and what shines is not their clothes but his own, white as the light.
cards.member_phrase: WHOLE
cards.member_sentence: Yahuah (the LORD) tells Moses to have the people wash their clothes and be ready, for he will come down upon the mountain.
cards.flag: Weak pair. The old note counts two days and a third day, which does not match Matthew's six days; I kept the Sinai coming-down and the washed clothes and said so plainly.

cards.prose: Daniel lifts up his eyes and sees a man clothed in linen with *his face as the appearance of lightning* (Daniel 10:6), and no strength is left in him. The three on the mountain are shown a face shining as the sun on the man standing before them, and when the voice comes they are on the ground. It is the same kind of sight.
cards.member_phrase: WHOLE
cards.member_sentence: Daniel sees a man clothed in linen, the shining figure whose sight takes the strength out of the one who looks.

cards.prose: On the mountain *his face did shine as the sun*, and John, who was one of the three, later sees *one like unto the Son of Adam* whose *countenance was as the sun shineth in his strength* (Revelation 1:16). It is the face the three saw shine, and John knew whose it was when he turned to look.
cards.member_phrase: one like unto the Son of Adam, clothed with a garment down to the foot
cards.member_sentence: John sees one like the Son of Adam in a long garment, the same shining Yahusha (Jesus) he saw on the mountain.

cards.prose: Paul says he was in the form of Elohim (God) and then *took upon him the form of a servant* (Philippians 2:7), made in the likeness of men. On the mountain the three are given a look at what the servant's form was covering, his face as the sun and his raiment white as the light.
cards.member_phrase: WHOLE
cards.member_sentence: Paul says Yahusha (Jesus) was in the form of Elohim (God) before he took on the form of a servant.

cards.prose: Moses died in Moab and was buried where *no man knoweth of his sepulchre* (Deuteronomy 34:6). Here the three see him standing and talking with Yahusha (Jesus), in what Yahusha (Jesus) afterward calls the vision. The man whose grave nobody can find is in the picture, and he is not silent.
cards.member_phrase: WHOLE
cards.member_sentence: Moses the servant of Yahuah (the LORD) died in Moab according to his word, so the man on the mountain is one who has died.

cards.prose: Elisha watched Elijah go up by a whirlwind and *he saw him no more* (2 Kings 2:12). Moses was buried and Elijah was taken up, and now the two who left the world by such different roads stand together on a mountain, talking with Yahusha (Jesus).
cards.member_phrase: there appeared a chariot of fire, and horses of fire, and parted them both asunder; and Elijah went up by a whirlwind into heaven
cards.member_sentence: Elijah is parted from Elisha by a chariot of fire and goes up by a whirlwind, so the other man on the mountain is one who was taken, not buried.

cards.prose: Matthew says only that they talked with him. Luke says what the talk was about, *his decease which he should accomplish at Jerusalem*. The Torah and the prophets are speaking with him about the very road he has told his disciples he must take, and they are not turning him from it.
cards.member_phrase: WHOLE
cards.member_sentence: Luke gives the subject of the talk with Moses and Elijah, his death at Jerusalem.

cards.prose: Moses and Elijah are among the men this verse speaks of, who obtained a good report through faith and *received not the promise*. They are seen talking with him, and the promise itself still waits, for Elohim (God) provided something better *that they without us should not be made perfect* (Hebrews 11:40).
cards.member_phrase: WHOLE
cards.member_sentence: The faithful of old, Moses and Elijah among them, have not yet received the promise, and they are not made perfect without us.

cards.prose: Peter says *three tabernacles*, and that is the Torah's own word for a feast: *The fifteenth day of this seventh month shall be the feast of tabernacles for seven days unto Yahuah (LORD)* (Leviticus 23:34). He reaches for booths on a mountain where the glory of Yahuah (the LORD) has just shown itself.
cards.member_phrase: WHOLE
cards.member_sentence: This verse opens the Torah's instruction on the feast of tabernacles, the dwelling in booths Peter's word calls to mind.
cards.flag: The target verse is only the opening clause; the feast itself is named in the next verse, so the prose quotes that verse.

cards.prose: The booths Peter wanted belong to a feast with a future. Zechariah has those left of the nations that came against Jerusalem going up *from year to year to worship the King* and *to keep the feast of tabernacles*, in the day when Yahuah (the LORD) is King over all the earth.
cards.member_phrase: shall even go up from year to year to worship the King, Yahuah Tseva'ot (LORD of hosts), and to keep the feast of tabernacles
cards.member_sentence: The feast of tabernacles is still kept in the day of the King, when the nations left alive go up to worship.

cards.prose: Peter wants to build three dwellings. John, who stood beside him, later writes that *the Word was made flesh, and dwelt among us* and that *we beheld his glory*. The tabernacle was already standing in front of Peter, in the man whose face was shining.
cards.member_phrase: And the Word was made flesh, and dwelt among us
cards.member_sentence: John says the Word dwelt among us and they beheld his glory, the glory the three beheld on the mountain.

cards.prose: Peter offered to put up three booths on the mountain, and what is promised at the end is a dwelling that Elohim (God) brings himself: *the tabernacle of Elohim (God) is with men*, and *they shall be his people*. The feast Peter reached for points to that day.
cards.member_phrase: Behold, the tabernacle of Elohim (God) is with men, and he will dwell with them, and they shall be his people
cards.member_sentence: At the end the tabernacle of Elohim (God) is with men and he dwells with them, the dwelling Peter's booths point toward.

cards.prose: These are the words that came from heaven at the Jordan, spoken again out of the cloud, with something added at the end. *Hear ye him* is the Father's word to the three who have just watched his Son talking with Moses and Elijah.
cards.member_phrase: WHOLE
cards.member_sentence: The Father's voice over the Son at the Jordan is the voice that speaks again out of the cloud.

cards.prose: In the wilderness Yahuah (the LORD) went in front of Yashar'el (Israel) by day in a pillar of cloud as their guide. A cloud comes over the three on the mountain and a voice comes out of it, and again the cloud is where the voice is found.
cards.member_phrase: went before them by day in a pillar of a cloud, to lead them the way
cards.member_sentence: Yahuah (the LORD) led Yashar'el (Israel) by a pillar of cloud, the cloud that speaks over the Son on the mountain.

cards.prose: When the cloud covered the tent, the glory of Yahuah (the LORD) filled the tabernacle, and *Moses was not able to enter into the tent of the congregation, because the cloud abode thereon* (Exodus 40:35). On the mountain a bright cloud overshadows them, and they fall on their faces.
cards.member_phrase: WHOLE
cards.member_sentence: The cloud covers the tent and the glory of Yahuah (the LORD) fills the tabernacle, the glory that overshadows the three.

cards.prose: At the dedication the cloud filled the house of Yahuah (the LORD), so that *the priests could not stand to minister because of the cloud* (1 Kings 8:11). The cloud that overshadows the three is that cloud, and they too cannot stand before it.
cards.member_phrase: WHOLE
cards.member_sentence: The cloud fills the house of Yahuah (the LORD) at its dedication, so that the priests cannot stand.

cards.prose: Isaiah promises a cloud by day and a flaming fire by night upon every dwelling place of mount Zion, in the day when the one who is left there *shall be called holy, even every one that is written among the living in Jerusalem* (Isaiah 4:3). The bright cloud over the three is that cloud, shown beforehand.
cards.member_phrase: will create upon every dwelling place of mount Zion, and upon her assemblies, a cloud and smoke by day, and the shining of a flaming fire by night
cards.member_sentence: Yahuah (the LORD) will make a cloud by day and a flaming fire by night over mount Zion, the glory covered by a defence.

cards.prose: Peter, who heard the voice on the mountain, later tells the people what it meant. Moses said a prophet like himself would be raised up from among the brethren, and *him shall ye hear in all things*. So *hear ye him* is no new command. It is Moses' own promise, and the man he promised is standing there with Moses himself beside him.
cards.member_phrase: A prophet shall Yahuah Elohaychem (the Lord your God) raise up unto you of your brethren
cards.member_sentence: Peter reads the Father's words from the cloud as Moses' promise of a prophet like himself, whom the people are to hear.

cards.prose: Peter says he was there. He calls himself and the others *eyewitnesses of his majesty* (2 Peter 1:16), and the voice he heard come *from the excellent glory* is the voice Matthew places in the bright cloud, spoken when they were with him on the holy mountain.
cards.member_phrase: when there came such a voice to him from the excellent glory
cards.member_sentence: Peter himself testifies that he heard the Father's voice from the excellent glory on the holy mountain.

cards.prose: Daniel falls on his face when the messenger comes near, and then *he touched me, and set me upright* (Daniel 8:18). The three fall on their faces in the same way, and Yahusha (Jesus) comes and touches them: *Arise, and be not afraid* (Matthew 17:7).
cards.member_phrase: when he came, I was afraid, and fell upon my face
cards.member_sentence: Daniel falls on his face before the messenger, the same fall of fear the three make on the mountain.

cards.prose: Ezekiel sees the brightness round about *as the appearance of the bow that is in the cloud*, falls on his face, and hears a voice that speaks. The three on the mountain hear a voice out of a bright cloud and fall on their faces. It is the same glory, and the same fall.
cards.member_phrase: This was the appearance of the likeness of the glory of Yahuah (LORD). And when I saw it, I fell upon my face, and I heard a voice of one that spake
cards.member_sentence: Ezekiel sees the glory of Yahuah (the LORD), falls on his face, and hears a voice speaking.

cards.prose: Isaiah sees the King and cries that he is undone, a man of unclean lips among a people of unclean lips. The three disciples fall down for the same reason, they have just heard the voice out of the glory, and the nearness of it lays a man flat before he can speak.
cards.member_phrase: for mine eyes have seen the King, Yahuah Tseva'ot (LORD of hosts)
cards.member_sentence: Isaiah cries woe at the sight of the King, the same undone fear the three show when the voice speaks.

cards.prose: John falls at his feet as dead, and he lays his right hand on him with *Fear not*. John was one of the three who fell on the mountain, and the hand and the words are the same: Yahusha (Jesus) *came and touched them, and said, Arise, and be not afraid* (Matthew 17:7).
cards.member_phrase: And when I saw him, I fell at his feet as dead. And he laid his right hand upon me, saying unto me, Fear not
cards.member_sentence: John falls as dead before him and is told Fear not, as he was raised on the mountain.

cards.prose: The sign of the prophet Jonah is the sign of his rising: *so shall the Son of Adam be three days and three nights in the heart of the earth* (Matthew 12:40). That is why the vision is to be kept quiet until the Son of Adam is risen from the dead.
cards.member_phrase: there shall no sign be given to it, but the sign of the prophet Jonah
cards.member_sentence: The only sign given to that generation is the sign of Jonah, the three days that the charge to silence looks toward.

cards.prose: He silences them twice. Once he charges them to tell no man he was the Messiah (Christ), and then *he must go unto Jerusalem, and suffer many things* (Matthew 16:21). Coming down the mountain he gives the date the silence ends, *until the Son of Adam be risen again from the dead*.
cards.member_phrase: WHOLE
cards.member_sentence: Yahusha (Jesus) charges the disciples to tell no man he was the Messiah (Christ), and goes on to speak of his death.

cards.prose: He said it of John before: *this is Elijah, which was for to come*. Yet on the way down he says Elijah *shall first come, and restore all things*, in the future. So John came in the pattern of Elijah, and the restoring is still in front of us.
cards.member_phrase: WHOLE
cards.member_sentence: Yahusha (Jesus) names John as Elijah, which was for to come, to those who will receive it.

cards.prose: Elijah's work cost him the favour of a king's house, and John's did too. He told Herod *It is not lawful for thee to have her* (Matthew 14:4), and Herod bound him. The one who comes in Elijah's pattern to restore is met by a ruler who does not want it restored.
cards.member_phrase: WHOLE
cards.member_sentence: Herod hears of Yahusha (Jesus) and takes him for John risen, the John he bound for speaking against his marriage.
cards.flag: The target verse is only the opening line; the point sits in the next verses about John, so I quoted verse 4.

cards.prose: Gabriel said John would go before him *in the spirit and power of Elijah*, turning the hearts of fathers back toward their children. John is Elijah's pattern at work, which is why Yahusha (Jesus) can say Elijah is come already and still speak of Elijah who shall first come and restore all things.
cards.member_phrase: And he shall go before him in the spirit and power of Elijah, to turn the hearts of the fathers to the children
cards.member_sentence: Gabriel says John will come in the spirit and power of Elijah, turning hearts and preparing a people.

cards.prose: Revelation gives the two witnesses Elijah's own marks: *These have power to shut heaven, that it rain not in the days of their prophecy* (Revelation 11:6), and fire out of their mouth. Yahusha (Jesus) says Elijah shall first come, and here is that pattern at work again further on.
cards.member_phrase: I will give power unto my two witnesses, and they shall prophesy a thousand two hundred and threescore days
cards.member_sentence: Two witnesses are given power and prophesy in sackcloth, carrying Elijah's marks into the days still ahead.
cards.flag: The old note calls this a second fulfilment of the Elijah pattern; I kept that and did not name who the two witnesses are.

cards.prose: Yahusha (Jesus) says Elijah shall *restore all things*, and Peter says heaven must receive him *until the times of restitution of all things*, which Elohim (God) has spoken by all his prophets. Peter stood on that mountain. The restoring is the same, and it is still waiting.
cards.member_phrase: until the times of restitution of all things, which Elohim (God) hath spoken by the mouth of all his holy prophets since the world began
cards.member_sentence: Peter says heaven keeps Yahusha (Jesus) until the times of restitution of all things, the restoring the prophets spoke.

cards.prose: Perverse is Moses' word from the song he taught Yashar'el (Israel), where a generation that corrupted itself, unmindful of the Rock that begat it, is named *a perverse and crooked generation*. Yahusha (Jesus) says it to the crowd at the foot of the mountain, and it grieves him.
cards.member_phrase: WHOLE
cards.member_sentence: Moses names the generation that corrupted itself a perverse and crooked generation, the word Yahusha (Jesus) uses.

cards.prose: *Faithless* here is this verse's *children in whom is no faith*, where Yahuah (the LORD) says he will hide his face to see their end. Now he is among them in the flesh, face and all, and still he asks how long he must be with them.
cards.member_phrase: for they are a very froward generation, children in whom is no faith
cards.member_sentence: Yahuah (the LORD) says of the froward generation that they are children in whom is no faith.

cards.prose: Moses' word is not alone. The psalm says what the fault was: *They kept not the covenant of Elohim (God), and refused to walk in his law* (Psalm 78:10). The rebuke is aimed at a generation that turned from the Torah, never at the Torah.
cards.member_phrase: a generation that set not their heart aright, and whose spirit was not stedfast with Elohim (God)
cards.member_sentence: The psalm calls the fathers a stubborn and rebellious generation that set not their heart aright.

cards.prose: *How long shall I suffer you* is the grief of the wilderness: *Forty years long was I grieved with this generation*, and the trouble was that they had not known his ways. The one who led them there is the one standing at the foot of the mountain asking how long.
cards.member_phrase: WHOLE
cards.member_sentence: Yahuah (the LORD) was grieved forty years with that generation, a people who err in heart and have not known his ways.

cards.prose: In the parable the kingdom is a grain of mustard seed, *the least of all seeds* (Matthew 13:32), which grows into a tree. Here faith is that seed, and the smallest of faith is enough to move a mountain. The smallness is the point in both places.
cards.member_phrase: WHOLE
cards.member_sentence: The kingdom of heaven is like a grain of mustard seed, the same seed Yahusha (Jesus) names for faith.

cards.prose: He says it a second time to the same men, at the fig tree, and gives the other half. Here the failure is *your unbelief*, and there the condition is *If ye have faith, and doubt not*. A mountain moved in both, but only by faith that does not waver.
cards.member_phrase: If ye have faith, and doubt not, ye shall not only do this which is done to the fig tree, but also if ye shall say unto this mountain, Be thou removed, and be thou cast into the sea; it shall be done
cards.member_sentence: Yahusha (Jesus) repeats the mountain saying after the fig tree withers, with the condition that they doubt not.

cards.prose: Paul takes up the same picture, faith enough to remove mountains, and says that without charity it is nothing. So the faith Yahusha (Jesus) asks for is no show of power. It is the kind of faith that sits beside love and is not mistaken for it.
cards.member_phrase: though I have all faith, so that I could remove mountains, and have not charity, I am nothing
cards.member_sentence: Paul says that all faith, even enough to remove mountains, is nothing without charity.

cards.prose: He says *when ye fast*, as something his hearers already do, and the Sermon says how it is done: not to be seen of men, but unto the Father, who *seeth in secret, shall reward thee openly* (Matthew 6:18). The fasting that goes with prayer is of that kind.
cards.member_phrase: when ye fast, be not, as the hypocrites, of a sad countenance
cards.member_sentence: Yahusha (Jesus) teaches that when his hearers fast, they do not do it to be seen.

cards.prose: Isaiah says what fast Yahuah (the LORD) chose: *to loose the bands of wickedness* and *to let the oppressed go free*. A boy who falls into fire and water is held by such a band, and the fast that goes with prayer is the kind that looses.
cards.member_phrase: to loose the bands of wickedness, to undo the heavy burdens, and to let the oppressed go free, and that ye break every yoke
cards.member_sentence: Isaiah says the fast Yahuah (the LORD) chose is loosing bands, undoing burdens and freeing the oppressed.

cards.prose: The practice he names to the disciples goes on after him. At Antioch they ministered to Yahuah (the LORD) and fasted, and in that time the Ruach HaKodesh (Holy Spirit) spoke and set Barnabas and Saul apart for the work.
cards.member_phrase: As they ministered to Yahuah (Lord), and fasted, the Ruach HaKodesh (Holy Spirit) said, Separate me Barnabas and Saul
cards.member_sentence: At Antioch the men fasted while they ministered, and the Ruach HaKodesh (Holy Spirit) set Barnabas and Saul apart.

cards.prose: Prayer and fasting go together again here. When Paul and Barnabas appointed elders in each place, they *prayed with fasting* and committed them to Yahuah (the LORD), so the two Yahusha (Jesus) joined on the mountain road are still joined in the work.
cards.member_phrase: WHOLE
cards.member_sentence: Paul and Barnabas pray with fasting when they appoint elders and commit them to Yahuah (the LORD).

cards.prose: He said it first plainly: he must go to Jerusalem, suffer many things, be killed, and be raised the third day. Now in Galilee he says it again, with the new word *betrayed*, and the whole company is exceeding sorry. The road has not changed since the mountain.
cards.member_phrase: he must go unto Jerusalem, and suffer many things of the elders and chief priests and scribes, and be killed, and be raised again the third day
cards.member_sentence: The first foretelling that he must go to Jerusalem, suffer, be killed and be raised the third day.
cards.flag: No passion thread exists for this chapter, so the card joins the thread for the verses it sits in.

cards.prose: Each telling adds a piece. Here it is that the Son of Adam will be betrayed into the hands of men, and on the way up it is named whose hands, *the chief priests and unto the scribes* (Matthew 20:18). The third day he shall rise is in both.
cards.member_phrase: WHOLE
cards.member_sentence: The third foretelling, made to the twelve on the road up to Jerusalem, names who will condemn him.
cards.flag: The target verse is only the introduction to the third foretelling; the content is in the next two verses, so I quoted verse 18.

cards.prose: Men hand him over, and Isaiah shows who is behind the handing over: Yahuah (the LORD) laid on him the iniquity of us all. And those it was laid for are *all we like sheep*, gone astray, each to his own way, the lost sheep he came to find.
cards.member_phrase: WHOLE
cards.member_sentence: Yahuah (the LORD) lays the iniquity of the sheep who have gone astray on the one who is betrayed.

cards.prose: The shepherd is struck and the sheep scattered, and the betrayal is the striking. But Zechariah does not stop there, for the next verse says *I will bring the third part through the fire, and will refine them as silver is refined* (Zechariah 13:9). The scattering is not the end.
cards.member_phrase: smite the shepherd, and the sheep shall be scattered: and I will turn mine hand upon the little ones
cards.member_sentence: The sword is called against the shepherd, the sheep are scattered, and Yahuah's (the LORD's) hand turns upon the little ones.

cards.prose: The collectors want the half shekel, and the money comes from this passage: every one numbered gives half a shekel after the shekel of the sanctuary, and *an half shekel shall be the offering of Yahuah (LORD)* (Exodus 30:13). He does not set the Torah aside, for he says the children are free and then has it paid.
cards.member_phrase: WHOLE
cards.member_sentence: This verse opens the Torah's instruction on the half shekel that each one numbered gives to the sanctuary.
cards.flag: The target verse is only the opening clause; the half shekel is in verse 13, so I quoted that verse.

cards.prose: Yahuah (the LORD) prepared a great fish for Jonah, and at Capernaum a fish is ready with a coin in its mouth. Peter is told to *take up the fish that first cometh up* (Matthew 17:27), and it comes to his hook as it came for Jonah. The fish does what it is told in both places.
cards.member_phrase: Now Yahuah (LORD) had prepared a great fish to swallow up Jonah
cards.member_sentence: Yahuah (the LORD) prepares a great fish, as he has one ready with the coin for Peter.

cards.prose: The kings' children are free, and a servant does not abide in the house for ever but the Son does. He says in John, *If the Son therefore shall make you free, ye shall be free indeed* (John 8:36). The freedom is the Son's place in his Father's house, and he pays the half shekel to that house anyway.
cards.member_phrase: WHOLE
cards.member_sentence: The servant does not abide in the house for ever, but the Son abides ever.

cards.prose: The children are free, and yet he sends Peter for the coin *lest we should offend them* (Matthew 17:27). Paul gives the same reason, that nobody is to set *a stumblingblock or an occasion to fall* before his brother. Free, and giving up the right so as not to trip someone.
cards.member_phrase: that no man put a stumblingblock or an occasion to fall in his brother’s way
cards.member_sentence: Paul asks that no man put a stumblingblock in his brother's way, the care that sends Peter for the coin.
cards.flag: Romans 14 sits inside a dispute about foods and days; I kept only the stumblingblock line and did not take it as reopening any commandment.
